Playbook.name: Perimeter — Host Exhibiting Multiple Attack Behaviors (Confirmed Compromise) - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: One source.ip triggered >=2 distinct FortiGate perimeter detections (24h/source suppressed) - a confirmed multi-behavior perimeter threat. Triage: a confirmed attacking source, or an internal source with unrelated perimeter alerts?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: A source with multiple distinct perimeter attack behaviors is a confirmed, active perimeter threat.

Assets.AssetType: Correlated across all JCB detection surfaces

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Elastic Security alerts index (.alerts-security.alerts-*). Correlation rules aggregate constituent alerts by a shared entity (host/user/source.ip). Fields: kibana.alert.rule.name, kibana.alert.severity, kibana.alert.risk_score, source.ip, host.name, user.name, event.module, @timestamp.
IMPORTANT: correlation must rest on a SHARED ENTITY, not mere time-proximity - these queries pivot on the entity and list the constituent alerts.

Signal.Name: Host Exhibiting Multiple Attack Behavior
Signal.Details: correlated alerts on a shared source.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance, not any single fact.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the correlated alerts on this source form a real multi-signal incident or coincidental unrelated alerts.

Step.name: List the constituent alerts for this entity
Step.Purpose: The set of distinct rules/severities on the shared entity shows whether a real multi-signal incident exists (correlation by ENTITY, not time).
Step.Query: FROM .alerts-security.alerts-* | WHERE source.ip == "192.168.228.82" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS alerts = COUNT(*), distinct_rules = COUNT_DISTINCT(kibana.alert.rule.name), rules = VALUES(kibana.alert.rule.name), max_risk = MAX(kibana.alert.risk_score), modules = VALUES(event.module) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Multiple DISTINCT FortiGate detections (sweep + C2 + exploitation) on one source = confirmed multi-behavior threat. An internal source with unrelated benign perimeter alerts is not - check whether internal or external.

Node.Condition: Multiple distinct perimeter attack behaviors on one source.
Node.Result: True Positive (Confirmed Perimeter Threat - block source, IR)

Node.Condition: The alerts are coincidental, unrelated, and individually benign/low-fidelity.
The constituent alerts are known-benign/tuned (e.g. the noisy rules pending tuning).

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-CORR-ALERTS to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: An internal source with unrelated perimeter alerts.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the constituent alerts are individually benign/unrelated; close as false_positive.
Treat as a confirmed multi-signal incident; contain the entity (isolate host / reset user / block source); open IR.
Reconstruct the chain from the constituent alerts.

Misconfiguration.Definition: Constituent alerts are known-noisy rules pending tuning.

Indicators.Item: Alerts from the noisy rules (spray/discovery) not yet tuned.

SOCAction.Item: Tune the constituent noisy rules; re-evaluate; document.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Review the constituent alerts; if a real incident, contain the entity.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Contain the entity (isolate/reset/block); open IR; reconstruct the chain.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Tune the noisy constituent rules to sharpen correlation fidelity; integrate the alert chain into IR.

QualityChecks.Check: Correlation rests on a shared entity, NOT time-proximity. Noisy constituent rules (spray/discovery) can inflate these - tune them.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Multi-signal incident contained; chain reconstructed; entity secured.
